newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK WATCHDOG COMMISSSION GETS TOUGH ON CHECKS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK WATCHDOG COMMISSSION GETS TOUGH ON CHECKS.

text.p: Greece's capital markets commission said on Monday the problem with Delta Securities' alleged fraudulent trading emerged not because of lax controls but as a result of tough supervision that started November 1.
"The problem that erupted on the Athens bourse came about as a result of stricter supervision that went into effect November 1 based on law 2396," it said in a statement.
"It did not come about because of lax contols as is widely presented by the press," it added.
The commisssion said the incident of a member brokerage failing to meet payment to the clearing house was of limited concern.
But, it said, the problem grew out of proportion because it exposed a series of imperfections in the exchange's clearing procedures.
After talks with the brokers association (SMEHA) it announced the following measures:
Payment to the clearing house will henceforth take place with cash or cashiers cheques. This measure already went into a effect last week, it said.
The exchange's supervisory authorities will continue their systematic checks and will bar from trade those member firms who owe securities to the clearing house -- do not deliver on time.

The commission has asked the Bank of Greece to liberalise credit to brokerages. This seeks to enable brokers to borrow funds to settle their payment obligations with the clearing house as well as to fund purchase of stock.
The clearing house will also withhold cash payments to brokers when they are even one day late in the delivery of shares.
The commission will set an interim transaction limit for brokerages based on their share capital, it said.
